subject: phy
title: Current Electricity
syllabus: Electric current, drift velocity, mobility and their relation with electric current; Ohm's law; electrical resistance; V–I characteristics of ohmic and non-ohmic conductors; electrical energy and power; electrical resistivity and conductivity; series and parallel combinations of resistors; temperature dependence of resistance; internal resistance, potential difference and emf of a cell; combination of cells in series and parallel; Kirchhoff's laws and their applications; Wheatstone bridge; metre bridge.

body: Current is the rate of flow of charge: I = \f{dq}{dt}. Unit: ampere (1 A = 1 C/s). If I changes with time, the charge is the AREA under the I–t graph: q = ∫I dt.
In a metal, free electrons move randomly at ~10^{5} m/s, but an electric field gives them a tiny average drift velocity (~10^{−4} m/s) opposite to E.

I = neAv_{d}
n = free electrons per m^{3}, A = cross-section.
Mobility μ = \f{v_{d}}{E} (m^{2}/V s). Current density J = \f{I}{A} = nev_{d} = σE (this is Ohm's law in "point" form), with conductivity σ = neμ = \f{1}{ρ}.
A bulb lights instantly although electrons crawl, because the FIELD travels through the wire at nearly the speed of light.

check.q: Drift speed of electrons in a copper wire is closest to :
check.why: Drift is very slow — of the order of 10^{−4} m/s.

body: Ohm's law: V = IR (at fixed temperature for ohmic conductors).

R = \f{ρL}{A}
ρ (resistivity) depends only on the MATERIAL and temperature — not on length or shape.
Stretching (volume fixed): L → nL makes A → A/n, so R → n^{2}R. If the radius becomes r/n, R → n^{4}R.
Cutting into n equal parts: each R/n; joined in parallel → R/n^{2}.
Metals: R_{t} = R_{0}(1 + αt), α > 0. Semiconductors: R falls as temperature rises. Alloys like manganin and constantan have tiny α — used for standard resistors.
Colour code (B B R O Y G B V G W = 0–9; gold ±5%, silver ±10%): first two bands digits, third the power of ten.

check.q: A wire is stretched to twice its length. Its resistance becomes :

body: Series: R = R_{1} + R_{2} + … (same current). Parallel: \f{1}{R} = \f{1}{R_{1}} + \f{1}{R_{2}} + … (same voltage). Two in parallel: \f{R_{1}R_{2}}{R_{1} + R_{2}}.
Symmetry trick: points at the same potential can be joined (or a resistor between them removed) without changing anything. Fold the circuit along its symmetry line.
Balanced Wheatstone bridge: if \f{P}{Q} = \f{R}{S}, the middle resistor carries no current — just remove it.

Must-know: triangle (side r) across two corners \f{2r}{3}; tetrahedron \f{r}{2}; cube edge \f{7r}{12}, face diagonal \f{3r}{4}, body diagonal \f{5r}{6}; hexagon with spokes, opposite corners \f{4r}{5}.
When nothing works: Kirchhoff — the sum of currents at a junction is 0 (charge conservation) and the sum of potential changes round a loop is 0 (energy conservation).

body:
A real cell = emf E in series with internal resistance r. With load R:
I = \f{E}{R + r}, terminal voltage V = E − Ir
While CHARGING (current forced in), V = E + Ir. Open circuit: V = E. Short circuit: I = E/r.

Series: E and r add (a reversed cell subtracts its E but still adds its r). Parallel:
E_{eq} = \f{E_{1}/r_{1} + E_{2}/r_{2}}{1/r_{1} + 1/r_{2}}, \f{1}{r_{eq}} = \f{1}{r_{1}} + \f{1}{r_{2}}
E_{eq} lies BETWEEN the two emfs.
n identical cells give the same current in series or parallel only when R = r.
Maximum power transfer: power in R is largest when R = r; then P_{max} = \f{E^{2}}{4r} and efficiency is only 50%.

check.q: A cell of emf 2 V, r = 1 Ω is connected to 3 Ω. Terminal voltage?

body:
P = VI = I^{2}R = \f{V^{2}}{R}
Joule heating H = I^{2}Rt.
A bulb rated (P_{0}, V_{0}) has fixed R = V_{0}^{2}/P_{0}. On voltage V: P = P_{0}(V/V_{0})^{2}.
In SERIES the bulb with larger R (lower wattage) glows brighter (same I, P = I^{2}R). In PARALLEL the higher-wattage bulb glows brighter (same V, P = V^{2}/R).
n identical bulbs in series on the mains draw P/n in total; in parallel nP.
Commercial unit: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^{6} J.

check.q: 60 W and 100 W bulbs (same rated voltage) in series — which glows brighter?
check.why: The 60 W bulb has larger R; in series P = I^{2}R is larger for it.

body: An ideal ammeter has zero resistance (in series); an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance (in parallel).
A real voltmeter R_{V} across a resistor R acts like R ∥ R_{V}, so it reads LESS than the true voltage.
Galvanometer → ammeter: small shunt S in parallel, S = \f{I_{g}G}{I − I_{g}}.
Galvanometer → voltmeter: large R in series, R = \f{V}{I_{g}} − G. To raise a voltmeter range from V_{1} to V_{2}: add (V_{2}/V_{1} − 1)R_{V} in series.

check.q: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter we connect :
check.why: A small shunt takes most of the current.

body: Balance (galvanometer reads zero): \f{P}{Q} = \f{R}{S}.

Meter bridge: a 100 cm uniform wire forms two arms. With X in the left gap, R in the right and null point at l cm from the left:
\f{X}{R} = \f{l}{100 − l}
The resistance per cm of the wire cancels — changing the wire does not move the null point. Swap X and R to cancel end errors.
Adding a resistor in parallel to one gap lowers that gap's resistance and moves the null point; use the new ratio to find the unknown.
Best accuracy near the middle (40–60 cm).

check.q: Null point at 40 cm with 6 Ω in the right gap. Left resistance?

body: A long uniform wire carries a steady current, so potential falls evenly along it: V ∝ l (potential gradient k = V/L).
At balance NO current flows from the cell under test, so the potentiometer measures the true emf: E = kl.

Internal resistance: balance l_{1} with the cell open, l_{2} with resistor R across it:
r = R(\f{l_{1}}{l_{2}} − 1)
With two different shunts use \f{R_{1}/(R_{1} + r)}{R_{2}/(R_{2} + r)} = \f{l_{1}}{l_{2}}.
Sensitivity improves with a smaller potential gradient (longer wire / smaller current).

formulas: L → nL ⇒ R → n^{2}R;  r → r/n ⇒ R → n^{4}R
traps: Resistivity is a property of the material — stretching changes R, not ρ.
Parallel cells: E_{eq} lies between the two emfs, it is never below both.
A reversed cell subtracts its emf but its internal resistance still ADDS.
Meter bridge: the left gap goes with the left length.
A real voltmeter always reads less than the true voltage.
Max power at R = r means only 50% efficiency.
In series the LOWER-wattage bulb glows brighter.
Changing the meter-bridge wire does not move the null point.

pyq.q: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistances 2 Ω and 1 Ω, respectively, are connected in series with an external resistance of 6 Ω. The total current in the circuit is I_{1}. Now the same two cells in parallel configuration are connected to same external resistance. In this case, the total current drawn is I_{2}. The value of (\f{I_{1}}{I_{2}}) is \f{x}{3}. The value of x is ______.

There are 'n' number of identical electric bulbs, each is designed to draw a power p independently from the mains supply. They are now joined in series across the mains supply. The total power drawn by the combination is :
An electric bulb rated 50 W – 200 V is connected across a 100 V supply. The power dissipation of the bulb is :
sol: Resistance stays the same: R = \f{V^{2}}{P} = \f{200^{2}}{50} = 800 Ω.
At 100 V: P = \f{100^{2}}{800} = 12.5 W (half the voltage → a quarter of the power).

pyq.q: To measure the internal resistance of a battery, potentiometer is used. For R = 10 Ω, the balance point is observed at l = 500 cm and for R = 1 Ω the balance point is observed at l = 400 cm. The internal resistance of the battery is approximately :
sol: The balancing length is proportional to the terminal voltage V = \f{ER}{R + r}.

pyq.q: The number of electrons flowing per second in the filament of a 110 W bulb operating at 220 V is : (Given e = 1.6 × 10^{−19} C)

Two resistors of 200 Ω and 400 Ω are connected in series with a battery of 100 V. A bulb rated at 200 V, 100 W is connected across the 400 Ω resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is ______ V.
sol: 400 Ω ∥ 400 Ω = 200 Ω, in series with 200 Ω → the 100 V splits equally.

pyq.q: A battery with EMF E and internal resistance r is connected across a resistance R. The power consumption in R will be maximum when :
sol: \f{dP}{dR} = 0 → (R + r)^{2} − 2R(R + r) = 0 → R = r (maximum power transfer).

pyq.q: Statement-I: The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs. Statement-II: The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.
sol: E_{eq} = \f{E_{1}r_{2} + E_{2}r_{1}}{r_{1} + r_{2}} — a weighted average, so it lies BETWEEN E_{1} and E_{2}. It is not smaller than both → Statement-I is false.
r_{eq} = \f{r_{1}r_{2}}{r_{1} + r_{2}} is smaller than each one → Statement-II is true.
o: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true

pyq.q: The electric current through a wire varies with time as I = I_{0} + βt, where I_{0} = 20 A and β = 3 A/s. The amount of electric charge crossed through a section of the wire in 20 s is :
A voltmeter with internal resistance of x Ω can be used to measure upto 20 V. In order to increase its measuring range to 30 V, the required modification is to ______.
sol: For 30 V: I_{g}(x + R) = 30 → x + R = \f{30x}{20} = 1.5x → R = \f{x}{2}, in SERIES (a series resistor takes the extra voltage).
o: connect resistor of \f{x}{2} Ω, in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of \f{x}{2} Ω, in parallel to voltmeter.
connect a resistor of x Ω in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of 2x Ω in parallel to voltmeter.

pyq.q: A meter bridge with two resistances R_{1} and R_{2} as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at 40 cm from the point P. The null point changed to 50 cm from the point P, when 16 Ω resistance is connected in parallel to R_{2}. The values of resistances R_{1} and R_{2} are ______.
sol: With 16 Ω across R_{2}, balance at the middle: R_{1} = \f{16R_{2}}{R_{2} + 16}.

pyq.q: Two resistance of 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in series with a battery of 4 V and negligible internal resistance. A voltmeter is used to measure voltage across 100 Ω resistance, which gives reading as 1 V. The resistance of voltmeter must be ______ Ω.
sol: The 200 Ω resistor has 4 − 1 = 3 V across it → I = \f{3}{200} A.
This current flows through 100 Ω ∥ R_{V}: \f{1}{3/200} = \f{200}{3} Ω.

pyq.q: The resistance per centimeter of a meter bridge wire is r, with X Ω resistance in left gap. Balancing length from left end is at 40 cm with 25 Ω resistance in right gap. Now the wire is replaced by another wire of 2r resistance per centimeter. The new balancing length for same settings will be at
sol: Balance needs \f{X}{25} = \f{l·r}{(100 − l)·r} — the resistance per cm cancels.
So the balance point does not depend on the wire: still 40 cm.

pyq.q: A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section 0.2 mm^{2} carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is α × 10^{−3} m^{2}/V.s. The value of α is : (electron concentration = 5 × 10^{28} /m^{3} and electron charge = 1.6 × 10^{−19} C)

When an external resistance of 5 Ω is connected across terminals of a cell, a current of 0.25 A flows through it. When the 5 Ω resistor is replaced by a 2 Ω resistor, a current of 0.5 A flows through it. The internal resistance of the cell is ______ Ω.

Two resistors of 100 Ω each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of 400 Ω resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is ______ V.
sol: Reading = 0.05 × 80 = 4 V (less than 4.5 V because the voltmeter draws current).

pyq.q: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance 2 Ω and 1 Ω, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of 1 A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be \f{α}{5} A. The value of α is ______.

In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances 2 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance l cm from the left. Now when an unknown resistance x is connected in parallel to 3 Ω resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance x is ______ Ω.
sol: \f{2}{3} = \f{l}{100 − l} → l = 40 cm; new null point at 50 cm.
At 50 cm the two gaps are equal: 2 = \f{3x}{3 + x} → 6 + 2x = 3x → x = 6 Ω.

pyq.q: A regular hexagon is formed by six wires each of resistance r Ω and the corners are joined to the centre by wires of same resistance. If the current enters at one corner and leaves at the opposite corner, the equivalent resistance of the hexagon between the two opposite corners will be
sol: Number the corners 0–5 and the centre C; current enters at 0 and leaves at 3. Put V_{0} = 1, V_{3} = 0 (take r = 1).
Symmetry: the centre sits halfway, V_{C} = \f{1}{2}; V_{1} = V_{5} = a and V_{2} = V_{4} = 1 − a.
Kirchhoff at corner 1: (1 − a) + (1 − a − a) + (\f{1}{2} − a) = 0 → a = \f{5}{8}.

pyq.q: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with 4 Ω resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with 12 Ω resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is ______ Ω.

For the two cells having same EMF E and internal resistance r, the current passing through the external resistor 6 Ω is same when both the cells are connected either in parallel or in series. The value of internal resistance r is ______ Ω.
sol: \f{2}{6 + 2r} = \f{1}{6 + r/2} → 12 + r = 6 + 2r → r = 6 Ω (equal currents happen exactly when R = r).

pyq.q: A wire of length 10 cm and radius √{7} × 10^{−4} m connected across the right gap of a meter bridge. When a resistance of 4.5 Ω is connected on the left gap by using a resistance box, the balance length is found to be at 60 cm from the left end. If the resistivity of the wire is R × 10^{−7} Ω m, then value of R is :

Wheatstone bridge principle is used to measure the specific resistance (S_{1}) of given wire, having length L, radius r. If X is the resistance of wire, then specific resistance is : S_{1} = X(\f{πr^{2}}{L}). If the length of the wire gets doubled then the value of specific resistance will be :
sol: Specific resistance (resistivity) is a property of the MATERIAL.
Doubling L doubles X, so X·πr^{2}/L stays the same: S_{1}.

pyq.q: A wire of resistance 20 Ω is divided into 10 equal parts. A combination of two parts are connected in parallel and so on. Now resulting pairs of parallel combination are connected in series. The equivalent resistance of final combination is ______ Ω.
sol: Each part = 2 Ω; two in parallel = 1 Ω.
Five such pairs in series = 5 Ω.

pyq.q: Resistance of a wire at 0 ºC, 100 ºC and t ºC is found to be 10 Ω, 10.2 Ω and 10.95 Ω respectively. The temperature t in Kelvin scale is ______.
A wire of resistance 9 Ω is bent to form an equilateral triangle. Then the equivalent resistance across any two vertices will be ______ ohm.
sol: Between two vertices: one side (3 Ω) in parallel with the other two (6 Ω) → \f{3 × 6}{9} = 2 Ω.

pyq.q: A wire of resistance R and length L is cut into 5 equal parts. If these parts are joined parallely, then resultant resistance will be :

A wire of resistance R is bent into an equilateral triangle and an identical wire is bent into a square. The ratio of resistance between the two end points of an edge of the triangle to that of the square is

When a potential difference V is applied across a wire of resistance R, it dissipates energy at a rate W. If the wire is cut into two halves and these halves are connected mutually parallel across the same supply, the same supply, the energy dissipation rate will become:
sol: Halves: R/2 each; in parallel → R/4.

pyq.q: A wire of resistance R is bent into a triangular pyramid as shown in figure with each segment having same length. The resistance between points A and B is R/n. The value of n is :
sol: Between two corners of a tetrahedron the other two corners are at the same potential (symmetry), so the segment joining them carries no current.
Left: three parallel paths: r, 2r, 2r → r ∥ r = \f{r}{2} = \f{R}{12} → n = 12.
